This is the first of the intercessions, and it is the Praised Station (al-Maqam al-Mahmud), as its explanation has already passed in Surah Subhan (at the commentary on verse 79). Then the Lord, exalted is He, comes to judge as He wills, and the angels come before Him in rows upon rows.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Hell is brought forward on that Day﴾. Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said in his Sahih: Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn Khalid al-Kahili, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah – that is Ibn Mas'ud – who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hell will be brought on that Day, having seventy thousand bridles, with each bridle seventy thousand angels dragging it."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, from Umar ibn Hafs, with the same chain. He also narrated it from Abd ibn Humayd, from Abu 'Amir, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from al-'Ala' ibn Khalid, from Shaqiq ibn Salama – who is Abu Wa'il – from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, as his own statement, and he did not raise it to the Prophet. Similarly Ibn Jarir narrated it from al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa, from Marwan ibn Mu'awiya al-Fazari, from al-'Ala' ibn Khalid, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah, as his own statement.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that Day man will remember﴾ meaning: his deeds and what he had sent forward in the far and recent past of his life. ﴿But how will remembrance benefit him?﴾ meaning: how will remembrance profit him? ﴿He will say: "Oh, would that I had sent forth for my life"﴾ meaning: he will regret what he had committed of sins, if he was a disobedient one, and will wish he had increased in acts of obedience, if he was an obedient one. As Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal said:

Ali ibn Ishaq narrated to us, 'Abdullah – meaning Ibn al-Mubarak – narrated to us, Thawr ibn Yazid narrated to us, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayra – and he was one of the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) – who said: "If a servant prostrated on his face from the day he was born until he died of old age in obedience to Allah, he would still regard it as insignificant on the Day of Resurrection, and he would wish that he were returned to the world so that he might increase in reward and merit."

Bahir ibn Sa'd also narrated it from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from 'Utba ibn 'Abd, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [Musnad (4/185).]

Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes﴾ meaning: there is no one whose punishment is more severe than the punishment of Allah for one who disobeyed Him. ﴿And none will bind as He binds﴾ meaning: and there is no one more severe in seizing and binding than the Zabaniyah (guardian angels of Hell) toward those who disbelieved in their Lord, Mighty and Majestic. This applies to the criminals among the creatures and the wrongdoers. As for the pure, tranquil soul, which is the calm, steadfast one that remains with the truth, it will be said to it: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord﴾ meaning: to His nearness, His reward, and what He has prepared for His servants in His Garden, ﴿well-pleased﴾ meaning: within itself, ﴿and pleasing﴾ meaning: it has been pleased with Allah, and Allah is pleased with it and has made it content. ﴿Enter among My servants﴾ meaning: among their number. ﴿And enter My Garden.﴾ This is said to it at the time of death, and also on the Day of Resurrection, just as the angels give good tidings to the believer at his death and when he rises from his grave, and likewise here.

Then the commentators differed as to who this verse was revealed about. Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it was revealed about 'Uthman ibn 'Affan. And from Buraydah ibn al-Husayb: it was revealed about Hamza ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, may Allah be pleased with him.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas: On the Day of Resurrection it will be said to the tranquil souls: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord﴾, meaning: your companion, which is its body that it used to inhabit in the world, ﴿well-pleased and pleasing﴾.

It is also reported from him that he used to recite it: "Enter among My servant and enter My Garden." Likewise Ikrimah and al-Kalbi said, and Ibn Jarir preferred it, but it is rare, and the first view is apparent, due to His saying: ﴿Then they are returned to Allah, their true Master﴾ [al-An'am: 62] and ﴿And that our return is to Allah﴾ [Ghafir: 43], meaning: to His judgment and standing before Him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abdullah al-Dashtaki narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from his father, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing﴾, he said: It was revealed while Abu Bakr was sitting, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, how beautiful this is!" He said: "Indeed, it will be said to you this." [Also narrated by Ibn Mardawayh and al-Diya al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtara, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/513).]

Then he said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I recited before the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing﴾, and Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Indeed this is good." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Indeed the angel will say this to you at death."

Likewise Ibn Jarir narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from Ibn Yaman, with the same. This is a fine mursal report. [Tafsir al-Tabari (30/122); also narrated by Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/513).]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafa narrated to us, Marwan ibn Shuja al-Jazari narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: Ibn 'Abbas died at al-Ta'if, and a bird came that was not seen in its form, and it entered his bier, then it was not seen coming out of it. When he was buried, this verse was recited at the edge of the grave, though it was not known who recited it: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, so enter among My servants and enter My Garden.﴾

Al-Tabarani narrated it from Abdullah ibn Ahmad, from his father, from Marwan ibn Shuja, from Salim ibn 'Ajlan al-Aftas, with it, and mentioned it. [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/290); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (9/285): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih."]

Al-Hafiz Muhammad ibn al-Mundhir al-Harawi, known as Shakkar, mentioned in his book "al-'Aja'ib," with his chain, from Qubath ibn Razin Abu Hashim, who said: I was taken captive in the lands of the Romans, and the king gathered us and presented his religion to us, on the condition that whoever refused would have his neck struck. Three of them apostatized, and a fourth came and refused, so his neck was struck, and his head was thrown into a river there. It sank in the water, then floated on the surface of the water, and it looked at those three and said: "O so-and-so, and O so-and-so, and O so-and-so," calling them by their names. Allah, exalted is He, says in His Book: ﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing, so enter among My servants and enter My Garden.﴾ Then it dove into the water, [he said,] and the Christians nearly became Muslim, the king's throne fell, and those three returned to Islam. He said: The ransom came from the Caliph Abu Ja'far al-Mansur, and we were freed.

Al-Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir narrated in the biography of Rawaha bint Abi 'Amr al-Awza'i, from her father: Sulayman ibn Habib al-Muharibi narrated to me, Abu Umama narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man: "Say: O Allah, I ask You for a soul that is tranquil in You, that believes in meeting You, is content with Your decree, and is satisfied with Your bestowal." [Tarikh Dimashq (p. 100), "Tarajim al-Nisa"; al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/118) through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd al-Ghaffar, from Rawaha bint 'Abd al-Rahman, with it.]

Then he narrated from Abu Sulayman ibn Zabr that he said: This hadith of Rawaha is one of its kind.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Fajr, and all praise is due to Allah [and His favor].
